overrides: the mission smoke's manual 1/60 s clock
the mission smoke's test placements of the production player body (each one listed in report.json under `placements`); the no-teleport run that produces the flight frames uses none
unknowns: the altimeter needle rates, the compass tape's period and scroll direction, the pip fill rule and the damage state→colour mapping (PartState::Damaged → yellow, Destroyed → red; the orangehilite set is never selected) are designed fits — the original's exact values are unmeasured, recorded in docs/findings/2026-10-20-m01-hud-art-instruments.md

the lowalt_on/stallwarning_on flags, the mgarrow/ggarrow ordnance arrows and the nitro_boost/nitro_charge needles have no measured driver: they keep their authored state (the flags hidden) and are reported in MissionHudArt.unknowns
the drawn dial radius (0.9 HUD units per measured face radius) and the 4:3 camera fit are designed capture fits to the owner's reference frames, not stored rows

the gun gauge's pip fill has no declared capacity in the weapon authority: it compares remaining rounds against remaining rounds, so the four ggindicator pips are lit until the bank runs dry — a designed all-or-nothing rule
the scripted smoke never damages the player, so the green → yellow/red zone material swap is composed and driven but only the intact green state is photographed

review.method: Acceptance suite run locally with `retail,gpu,audio` (CS_GAME_DIR, CS_ENGINE_IMAGE): the owner's own command `cs --cs-path $CS_GAME_DIR --mission M01 --smoke-seconds 45 --capture-dir private/evidence/PARITY2-M01-HUD-ART` drove the same windowed composition the owner plays on this machine's GPU — through the launch cinematic — and wrote real framebuffer PNGs plus report.json with its scripted checks passing (`passed:true`, `human_play:false`). A second, no-teleport run (`--smoke-no-teleport`) flew the measured start pose continuously — never moving the player (`player_teleported:false`, `placements:[]`) — and wrote the in-flight frames at the fixed capture ticks (`frame_01500_flight_25s.png`, `frame_04200_flight_70s.png`), which is also the path the Flight Check hold covers: the mesh cluster's camera stays off while the check screen is pending and draws after Fly Mission. The cited HUD frame (`frame_*_hud.png`) shows the original gauge cluster drawn from the measured `instruments.zrd` placements and the `player > player_pfighter > cockpit1 > gauges` subtree of `zbd/planes.zbd` — dial faces, needles, the damage silhouette's four zones, missile/gun pips and glyph quads, the nitro gauge and the compass tape — plus the decoded `rcircle` reticle from `zbd/rimage.zbd`, where the text/CSS stand-ins stood down. The retail test composes M01 headless and asserts the cluster at once: the seven measured placements, one HUD root plus one dedicated overlay camera on the HUD render layer, ~30 mesh parts layered, and every measured live element carrying its marker (3 needles, the compass tape, 4 damage zones, 12 pips, 20 glyph cells, 2 flags, 2 arrows, 2 nitro needles). The runs are automated, never `human_play`, and no original executable ran. This harness derives every field from the recorded log, production discovery of $CS_GAME_DIR, the smokes' reports and the hashes of those artifacts. LIMITS: the altimeter rates, tape period, pip fill and damage-colour mappings are designed (unmeasured); the lowalt/stall flags, ordnance arrows and nitro needles have no measured driver and keep their authored state; the gun pips have no declared capacity so they light all-or-nothing; and the scripted smoke never damages the player, so only the zones' intact green is photographed. Validated with tools/validate_evidence.py (structure and artifact hashes, exit 0); --require-pass reports the recorded follow-up unknowns as unresolved issues, which stand as this task's honest limitations rather than being emptied to pass the gate.
